stories.title: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter
stories.reason: Anthropic's own Frontier Red Team research: small open-weight models (GLM-5.2, Qwen3.5-9B) can already chain inference-setup + propagation steps to self-replicate across low-security IoT devices (8/8 GCP-emulated nodes in 4/5 trials); capability trend projects commodity-scale models hit this bar by end of 2026. Concrete measured attack-success numbers, primary source, directly on the AI x cyber line.
key_facts: Qwen3.5-9B got inference running on 8 of 9 tested hardware types
GLM-5.2 spread end-to-end to all 8 nodes in 4 of 5 trials (7/8 in the fifth) in a firewalled-VPC worm test
Gemma4-26B-A4B ran distributed across 15 $55 Android TV boxes via pipeline parallelism at ~0.39 tok/s
Open-weight <=30B models' Epoch Capabilities Index rises ~13.7 pts/yr (R^2=0.95), projecting GLM-5.2-level replication ability by end of 2026
Passing notes between generations raised Qwen3.5-9B inference-setup success from 45% to 61-84%

stories.title: Codex CLI installs a persistent, self-updating background daemon by default
stories.reason: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.157.0 silently ships daemon_auto_start=true: opening a session spawns a persistent codex app-server --managed-daemon that outlives the window, copies a ~374MB package tree to ~/.codex, and self-updates hourly, restarting mid-turn. Undocumented in release notes; GitHub issue #48195 (open, no OpenAI response) has commenters calling it malware-like and rolling back company licenses. 475 HN points -- already widely seen, which is exactly what makes it a headline.
key_facts: Daemon persists after all Codex windows close; survives until `daemon stop` or reboot
Copies ~374MB platform package (codex, bwrap, zsh, rg) into ~/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon/releases/<version>/
Update-check loop runs 5 min after start then hourly, can restart backend mid-turn
Opt-out via `codex features disable daemon_auto_start` or config.toml, undocumented as of Oct 12
`daemon stop` bug: leaves the update loop still running

stories.title: Zod 4.6.6 compromised by malware?
stories.reason: Verified directly: zod/@zod/mini 4.6.6's commit diff adds a minified meta.test.mjs wired into preinstall that resolves an Ethereum-contract-stored domain (EtherHiding-style C2), fetches a base64 setup+payload bundle, and executes it via a data: URL import at install time -- classic npm supply-chain backdoor pattern, no maintainer explanation in the commit. zod is one of the most widely depended-on JS/TS validation libraries, including as the schema layer in a lot of LLM tool-calling/agent-framework code, so the blast radius if confirmed malicious is large even though this is pure-cyber rather than AI research itself.
key_facts: Commit d821685 bumps zod/@zod/mini 4.6.5->4.6.6, titled 'Fix bugs and improve performance'
Adds meta.test.mjs (minified) wired via package.json `preinstall` hook in both packages
meta.test.mjs queries an Ethereum contract via public RPC, decodes the result as a domain, fetches https://<domain>/loader
Response contains base64 setup script + base64 payload; setup is run via a data: URL import, payload written to temp dir then deleted
release.yml changed to trigger on any push to main touching version files, removing a comment that said a version bump alone doesn't publish and a maintainer must approve the npm release
